records.name: Laura Faustini
records.bio: Faustini co-authored the 2017 study of the Fondazione Scienza e Tecnica collection in Florence. The article provides the 118-object historical sequence, the 111 surviving-model count, Marchi’s role, purchase evidence, restoration history and technical-analysis results.

records.name: Stefania Lotti
records.bio: Lotti co-authored the 2017 Florence collection study that reconstructs acquisition, catalogue sequence, survival, restoration and technical analysis. It is the principal modern source behind the project’s object-level Florence module.

records.name: Helen Shaddock
records.bio: Shaddock’s 2015 collection-visit account records approximately fifty Blaschka sea-anemone models at Newcastle and describes their scientific purpose. The project retains the account as a secondary documentary checkpoint rather than an official inventory.
records.open: The reported count remains a secondary-source figure until matched to an institutional register.

records.name: Paolo Viscardi
records.bio: Viscardi’s 2019 NatSCA article provides a published Liverpool object anchor, identifying a World Museum Blaschka specimen with catalogue number 93. His wider collections work also connects the project to surviving Irish and British holdings.

records.name: Kate McNally
records.bio: McNally’s 2025 Tufts Archival Research Center account reconstructs the collection from Barnum’s 1885 purchase through Corning custody, documentary rediscovery, restoration and return. It also supplies the current archival count of twenty-two models and identifies the Biology department records behind the story.

records.name: Jonathan Heath
records.bio: Heath’s Corning Museum of Glass account reconstructs the later Tufts custody story through the 1960s correspondence, the 1972 flood, recovery of ten models, conservation and their 2007 return. The article is one of the principal institutional narratives for the case.

records.name: Helene Ragovin
records.bio: Ragovin’s 2009 Tufts account records the rediscovery and return of the university’s Blaschka models, including the Dana Laboratory closet find and Stephen Koob’s discussion of treatment. The project uses it as a contemporary institutional reconstruction with oral-history elements.

records.name: Kerstin Barndt
records.bio: Barndt co-curated the 2017 Museum of Vitreous Ecology project at Michigan. The exhibition research brought together approximately seventy-eight marine models, fragments, teaching history and the later displacement of glass models by newer visual technologies.
records.open: The proposed Harvard/Agassiz route for part of the Michigan collection remains a curatorial hypothesis rather than closed provenance.

records.name: Alice Goff
records.bio: Goff co-curated the 2017 Museum of Vitreous Ecology project at Michigan. The research documented the surviving marine models, their fragmented condition, two acquisition strata and their changing status as teaching objects and historical artifacts.
records.open: The proposed Harvard/Agassiz route for part of the Michigan collection remains a curatorial hypothesis rather than closed provenance.
